correctness.rationale: The conditional hub hazard is exact because, before first hub elimination and with k>=4 rim vertices, hub degree=h+k-1 strictly exceeds rim degree=h+2. A rim pivot adds exactly one chord and retains clique–cycle shape; the first hub pivot adds k(k-3)/2 rim clique edges, after which all remaining vertices are a clique. This yields the finite distribution. Beta-binomial exact moments prove q=1, uniform asymptotics of p_k and survival prove q=2,3,4+ rates and tail; exact graph-state recurrence and permutations passed 491 independent finite checks. No enumeration is used as a proof of infinite assertions.

value.rationale: The join of a small clique and large cycle is a controlled sparse-Cholesky ordering benchmark. Exact fill count directly informs factor sparsity; the new finite law separates optimal, quadratic, linear, logarithmic and bounded excess risk as candidate count increases. Limiting q=2,3 laws have infinite mean despite finite-sample expectations, explaining rare catastrophic fill outcomes that typical experiments miss. This is an all-size natural invariant and a sharp structural power-of-choice classification, not a routine rephrasing of existing fill graph definitions.
